answer.note: I'm choosing A (dogwhistle/study.py) and B (dogwhistle/heldout.py), not the incoming A and C. The ref files are identical and give no file-specific priority, so I chose from the code. Only study.py:314 and heldout.py:343 have a two-stage `verify_history(seal, ledger, reveal, ...)`. Each checks prereg->seal and seal->ledger ordering. Visibility.py:191 has a single-stage `_verify_history` that checks only prereg->ledger, so it is not the two-arm verifier. Honest.py:175 also has a single-stage `_verify_history`, which I did not read. Neither candidate currently does what the request describes. Both use `git merge-base --is-ancestor`, which passes when the two commits are equal, so equal commits are not rejected. Neither checks that the ledger-seal commit changed only its public digest file. They only compare the digest file's content at each commit. Suggested 60 minutes: study.py 25, heldout.py 25, visibility.py 7, honest.py 3. Within study.py and heldout.py, spend the time on the verification function and the tests (tests/test_study.py, tests/test_heldout.py). Check whether the request is for a new check or for a verifier I missed. I only read the verification functions, not the full files.
